plan: [Game is a 3-player third-price auction (winner pays the lowest bid). With i.i.d. uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Bayes–Nash equilibrium bidding rule is b(v)=2v, which maximizes long-run expected payoff by balancing win probability and expected minimum payment (from the first-order condition on expected utility). Follow that equilibrium to maximize expected profit across rounds. With my private value $9, the equilibrium bid is 2*9 = $18.]

[I have value $9. In this 3-bidder, third-price (winner pays the lowest) auction, bidding my value guarantees I only win when both opponents bid below $9, so payment will be < $9 and I never incur a loss. With no past rounds or info, overbidding risks paying >$9 if both opponents bid above $9. I'll bid my value $9.]

[Third-highest = the lowest of the three bids, so my bid only affects whether I win. Assuming opponents bid near their values (uniform 0–49), raising my bid increases win probability faster than it raises expected payment. For v=34 the expected payoff is maximized at the practical upper bound, accepting the small risk of a loss if both opponents bid above 34. I will bid at the top of the value range to maximize long-run profit.]
